Subject: AtlasGRC / Redwood: evidence ingestion options for pen test + SOC2

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. AtlasGRC is onboarding Redwood as a verified partner so our customers can see pen test and SOC2 artifacts directly in our compliance console. We ran the checklist and have two immediate asks:

1) How can PenCheck deliver signed/preserved penetration test artifacts into AtlasGRC (S3, API push, or direct upload)? We need to understand the canonical ingestion path.
2) Retention & access controls: we need to confirm how long evidence will be available and who can retrieve it. We also need assurance around encryption-in-flight and at-rest and key control responsibilities.

I attached our standard onboarding form (Atlas_Onboarding_Form.xlsx) with fields for endpoint types, required metadata, and sample file naming conventions.

Can we set a 30-min sync with your security/ops folks tomorrow? I copied Samira from PenCheck — they are our preferred pen test vendor for this engagement.

Thanks,
Kelly Park

Subject: Re: AtlasGRC / Redwood: evidence ingestion options for pen test + SOC2

Hi Kelly — really glad to connect on this. Short answers up front: we can support both time-limited pre-signed S3 uploads and an API push model. We typically recommend the pre-signed S3 flow for large artifact bundles (pen-test reports, pcap, raw logs) and a lightweight metadata push to the GRC to index artifacts.

Notes on the flow we propose:
- PenCheck uploads encrypted tarballs to a tenant-specific S3 prefix using pre-signed PUTs; each upload emits a webhook to AtlasGRC with manifest metadata (artifact_id, checksum, scope, report_type).
- Redwood retains the artifact for the agreed retention period (configurable per-account) and optionally mirrors a read-only copy to Atlas if they prefer direct storage.
- KMS-managed server-side encryption is used by default; we support customer-managed keys on private deployments.

I attached a short sketch (proposed-evidence-flow.md) mapping roles and webhook payloads.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min technical sync (I can host) — Fri 07/10 10:00 PT or 14:00 PT; which works for you?
2) Vivek will review data classification & retention and confirm required DPA clauses.
3) If Atlas wants direct read access, we can grant a scoped IAM role for Atlas service accounts.

Vivek/Monica — adding you to confirm security controls and CS handoffs.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 19:45:30 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasGRC / Redwood: evidence ingestion options for pen test + SOC2

Thanks Kelly / Hannah — a few security points to lock before we enable any automated ingestion: 

1) Data classification: Pen test artifacts that include customer-identifying data must be redacted prior to submission. PenCheck should provide a metadata flag in the manifest that indicates whether the artifact contains PII.
2) Key management: for hosted customers we use Redwood KMS; for Private/VPC we require a customer-managed CMK. If Atlas wants read access, we need a documented key access policy (no cross-tenant decrypt).
3) Retention: Redwood's default retention for partner-delivered artifacts is 90 days unless the customer requests longer. Atlas and the customer must approve any extension.
4) Auditability: each artifact ingest will create an immutable audit entry (who uploaded, manifest, checksum, IP) stored for SOC2 purposes. We will provide Atlas read-only audit hooks for validated cases.

Operational requests: 
- PenCheck should deliver a signed manifest (SHA256) and a signed PDF of the pen test summary (PAdES or similar) so we can assert provenance.
- We need DocuSign copies of the DPA + any prospect-specific NDAs before enabling ingestion (please upload to the shared Drive link).

I can join the call tomorrow and review the KMS options and audit hook.

-Vivek
Head of Security — Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Hi all — Samira from PenCheck here. We're set up to produce:
- An encrypted tar.gz per engagement (AES-256), signed manifest.csv (SHA256) and a signed summary PDF.
- We can either upload directly using pre-signed PUTs or push to your API endpoint (you'll need a long-lived token for automation).

Two clarifications from our side: 
1) Scope verification: to ensure we map artifacts to the right customer in Atlas, we need a canonical identifier (account_id or customer_email) — please confirm which Atlas field we should populate.
2) Sanitization: we can run a redaction pass but need a checkbox in the workflow to indicate whether full raw captures are permitted.

Attached a current delivery manifest template (pencheck-inventory.csv). We can sign NDAs/DPA via DocuSign; please share the envelope link.
